statements.context: Essay arguing that psychopharmacology was a marketing brand created by Arthur Sackler and that psychiatric drugs 'don't do much'. After calling the drug-first era a tragic waste, the author asserts a counter-revolution toward interventional care (ECT, neuromodulation, psychedelic medicine) is brewing.
statements.note: Borderline: present-progressive claim implying a coming shift from psychopharmacology to interventional brain medicine.

statements.quote: It will inform and educate and will even lead some readers who may be suffering from mental health issues to durable remission of their symptoms.
statements.context: Closing of the Faust essay. 'This book' is the author's own book project on how psychiatry got here and where it is going. He predicts the book will lead some suffering readers to durable remission of their symptoms.
statements.note: Own-product claim about the author's book/newsletter; coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: I wrote earlier this year about my prediction that ADA will be brought to bear in the fight for accessible mental health care.
statements.context: Health policy update on the DOJ's first ADA settlement resolving employment discrimination based on alcohol use disorder. The author restates his earlier 2023 prediction (from his Perez v. Sturgis article) that the Americans with Disabilities Act will be used as an enforcement tool for access to mental health care.
statements.note: Restatement of an earlier call; the post treats the DOJ settlement as supporting evidence.

statements.quote: it follows that reasonable accommodations are also due to those with alcohol use disorder…and it might follow other psychiatric disabilities.
statements.context: After quoting the DOJ settlement (alcohol use disorder is an ADA-covered disability), the author infers that reasonable accommodations are due for AUD and might extend to other psychiatric disabilities. He then applies this to payer 'fail first' policies (NQTLs) and access to SAINT neuromodulation.
statements.note: Conditional legal inference; anticipates ADA accommodation claims extending to psychiatric disabilities and payer policies.

statements.quote: You can expect people to leave when you make a line of work miserable
statements.context: Essay using Richard III to discuss burnout, strikes and private equity in medicine. The author claims that making health care work miserable will drive physicians and nurses out of the field.
statements.note: General truism applied to the health workforce; borderline, logged for recall.

statements.quote: that doesn't get replaced overnight. It doesn't get replaced in a decade.
statements.context: The author argues that every burned-out doctor, completed suicide, or early retirement removes millions of dollars of training and tens of thousands of hours of experience, and that this lost clinical expertise will not be replaced within a decade.
statements.note: Claim about the recovery time of lost health workforce expertise.

statements.quote: The more we push, the more people will run for the exits.
statements.context: Author's claim about physician and nurse attrition: as the system pushes clinicians harder (private equity ownership, unsafe conditions, strikes), more of them will leave medicine, and 'the house of medicine is no re-entry'.
statements.note: Trend claim about health workforce exits.

statements.quote: We will all survive without private equity investors.
statements.context: Discussing 70,000 Kaiser nurses on strike and UK doctors' strikes, the author predicts society will survive without private equity investors in health care, in contrast to the consequences of losing doctors and nurses.
statements.note: Rhetorical contrast asserting private equity is dispensable to health care.

statements.quote: Very few of us will survive the kinds of predictable causes of early death that will commonly befall us if we let all the doctors and nurses quit.
statements.context: Conditional warning: if doctors and nurses are allowed to quit en masse (strikes, burnout, private equity), predictable causes of early death (appendicitis, accidents, infections, psychiatric emergencies) will kill many people.
statements.note: Conditional ('if we let all the doctors and nurses quit'); extreme framing.

statements.quote: This is the beginning of a remarkable change in the treatment of psychiatric disorders.
statements.context: Post celebrating Medicare NTAP (new technology add-on payment) approval for SAINT (Stanford Accelerated Intelligent Neuromodulation Treatment) in the inpatient setting and AMA category III CPT codes for outpatient use. The author predicts these payment pathways mark the start of a remarkable change in psychiatric treatment.
statements.note: Author is a SAINT provider (Fermata) and advocated for the NTAP; own-interest claim.

statements.quote: It opens the door for every breakthrough treatment to get additional payment models in the future. To be very clear, this is how psychedelic medicine will be paid for.
statements.context: The author claims the NTAP precedent for SAINT opens the door for other breakthrough treatments to get add-on payment models, and states that psychedelic medicine will be paid for through the same Medicare payment mechanism.
statements.note: Compound: general claim about breakthrough treatments plus a specific call on how psychedelic medicine will be reimbursed.

statements.quote: It's a huge leap forward. More are coming
statements.context: Close of the NTAP post. After urging advocacy for SAINT coverage in every setting, not just hospitals, the author says more coverage advances are coming.
statements.note: Vague; 'More are coming' refers to further payment or coverage advances for rapid-acting treatments.

statements.quote: Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment 2024 will be the hot party, with all the innovators from the front lines speaking!
statements.context: Promotion of the author's own conference (RAMHT 2024) on January 7, the night before the JPM healthcare conference; he predicts it will be 'the hot party' with front-line innovators speaking.
statements.note: Own-event promotion; coder may mark CONTROL (RAMHT).

statements.quote: If you've enjoyed hearing Jazz and I talk, there'll be more of it.
statements.context: Podcast outro after a conversation with Jazz Glastra, senior director at BrainFutures; the author promises more such conversations on the podcast.
statements.note: Content promise for the author's own podcast; coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: He and other exciting innovators will be there and talking to each other and to you at this reception.
statements.context: Podcast outro announcing Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment 2024 (January 7, San Francisco, right before the JPM Health Conference), co-sponsored by BrainFutures. The author says Grady Hannah (CEO of Nightware) and other innovators will attend.
statements.note: Own-event announcement; coder may mark CONTROL (RAMHT).

statements.quote: if you wanted to prevent schizophrenia, the easiest thing to do, in quotes around the word easiest, is get young people not to smoke any cannabis. That would prevent a lot of schizophrenia. Good luck with that, by the way.
statements.context: Podcast conversation with Jazz Glastra about prevention. Citing data (Christoph Correll, spelled 'Carell' in the transcript) on ultra-high-risk individuals converting to schizophrenia, the author claims reducing youth cannabis use would prevent a lot of schizophrenia, while doubting such a reduction can be achieved. Restated at the end: 'You could prevent schizophrenia by reducing the rates of cannabis use.'
statements.note: Conditional counterfactual claim plus skepticism about implementation ('Good luck with that'); borderline forecast.

statements.quote: A Denial of Objective Reality is Here 👏 Not 👏 Leaving!
statements.context: Section heading in a satirical essay on George Santos's indictment, riffing on Santos's own Bluesky arrival post ('The conservatives are here and we aren't leaving'). The author's thesis is that some people treat their inner reality as the only reality and that this denial of objective reality is a persistent feature, not a passing one.
statements.note: Rhetorical heading in a self-described satire post; borderline trend claim that denial of objective reality will persist.
